definition_issue: FC-ROUTE needs no contested fare ('made the trip longer and/or raised the fare'), so a slow-trip complaint is an FC type although EX is defined as 'no contested charge'; CW-DRIVERNOSHOW's 'was uncontactable' also reads onto a driver who did arrive. CLS-02's 'first stated issue' fallback then ranks a contextual remark (lateness) above the trip-duration, drop-off and cash issues.

evidence.quote: the driver arrived about 15 minutes late and did not respond to her messages beforehand
I told him I wasn't refusing to pay
otherwise the primary claim is the one contesting the largest charge; otherwise the first stated issue

reason: Nothing in the text contests a charge or asks for a remedy, so CLS-02 falls back to the first stated issue (late, unresponsive driver) and CLS-03 makes it a non-dispute. I change my blind FC-ROUTE, which wrongly treated the slow trip as implicitly contesting the fare.

definition_issue: CW-NOSHOW requires that the driver canceled 'because the rider did not show up', but the text gives no reason, and CW-DRIVERNOSHOW's exclusion sends every charged driver cancellation to CW-NOSHOW by default. SE-CONDUCT has no definition, so a yelling driver is kept out of SE only by CLS-01's word list.

evidence.quote: The driver also cancelled the booking, but Ms [NAME] was still charged a cancellation fee.
The rider contests a cancellation fee charged after the DRIVER canceled the trip because the rider did not show up.
Any case where the rider was charged a fee (classify by that fee: CW-RIDERCANCEL or CW-NOSHOW).

reason: The driver canceled and the rider contests the S$4.30 fee, which is the CW-NOSHOW path. Yelling is rudeness (EX-FEEDBACK), not CLS-01 language.

evidence.quote: he wanted to drop me off in the rain when there's a shelter right in front?
Location problem reported without contesting any charge.

reason: A drop-off point complaint with no charge or remedy at issue is EX-LOCATION, with the rudeness as an EX-FEEDBACK secondary.

definition_issue: CW-NOSHOW vs CW-RIDERCANCEL turns on who canceled, which this text only implies, and no rule says how to classify when the canceling party is unstated.

evidence.quote: he don't want to cancel the booking!
showing she was charged S$5.30 for the cancellation
The rider contests a cancellation fee charged after the RIDER canceled

reason: The driver refused to cancel, so the S$5.30 fee most plausibly followed the rider's own cancellation (CW-RIDERCANCEL). Trip logs should confirm the canceler, since CW-NOSHOW is the other adjudication path.

definition_issue: No type for refusal of service or disability discrimination, and SE-CONDUCT is undefined, so it is unclear whether a discriminatory refusal belongs in SE (human triage) or stays a CW/EX matter.

evidence.quote: He was there but drove off when he saw I was standing and talking to someone in a wheelchair
I did screenshot and lodge a complaint, and they gave a voucher
no fee was charged to the rider; the rider seeks redress or reports the driver

reason: No fee was charged, the driver drove off and canceled late, and the complaint produced a voucher, so CW-DRIVERNOSHOW with is_dispute true. Folding the refusal into the same claim instead of my EX-FEEDBACK secondary is acceptable, since it is one event.

definition_issue: SE-CONDUCT has no definition, so whether shouting or scolding is 'inappropriate behavior' (SE) or EX-FEEDBACK rests only on CLS-01's word list.

evidence.quote: scolded them for not knowing the rules
The driver should be asking instead of shouting (at us) and driving off.
otherwise the first stated issue

reason: No fee or remedy is mentioned and the first stated issue is the scolding, so EX-FEEDBACK with the drive-off as a CW-DRIVERNOSHOW secondary.

definition_issue: No leaf for a driver demanding extra or off-app payment (commission here, S$30 in C18, S$5 'VIP' in C19), so such demands scatter across FC-PAYMENT, FC-SURCHARGE and FC-OTHER.

evidence.quote: He was being intrusive, racist and threatened my safety
The driver then insisted that she paid his commission
A safety claim (CLS-01) is always the primary claim

reason: Threat language triggers CLS-01 and the religious and racist hostility is the primary SE-CONDUCT claim, with SE-DRIVING secondary. Recording the commission demand as FC-PAYMENT rather than my FC-OTHER is defensible.

definition_issue: CLS-03's safety exception names only CLS-01 (a word list), while CLS-02 treats any SE claim as 'a safety claim (CLS-01)'; SE leaves raised without listed words (SE-TERMINATED, SE-MISMATCH, SE-RECORDING) can therefore be sent to normal support despite their TRIAGE_TO_HUMAN scope.

evidence.quote: the driver stopped the car and asked her to get out
Ride terminated after the trip started
routed to normal support, unless CLS-01 applies
A safety claim (CLS-01) is always the primary claim

reason: SE-TERMINATED is right, but is_dispute=false lets CLS-03 send a mid-trip ejection to normal support, against the leaf's TRIAGE_TO_HUMAN scope. The KB treats the claim as a CLS-01 safety claim for primacy, then denies it the CLS-01 exception, which is inconsistent.

evidence.quote: The location service are a bit laggy
You just get a blank screen: the app does not work.
App or tracking problem

reason: No charge is contested; the first stated issue (laggy location) and the blank help screen are app problems, with rating and driver feedback as secondaries.

definition_issue: CW-DRIVERNOSHOW covers a rider who only 'reports the driver' (BACKLOG scope), but CLS-03 sends a claim with no charge and no remedy to normal support, so the type and the rule disagree on where such cases go.

evidence.quote: the vehicle whose driver accepted the ride remained in the same position on the map and was not moving
caught the driver eating at a coffee shop
no fee was charged to the rider; the rider seeks redress or reports the driver

reason: The driver never came and no fee was charged, which is CW-DRIVERNOSHOW. With no remedy requested, CLS-03 makes it a non-dispute.

definition_issue: SE-CONDUCT has no definition and its label ('inappropriate behavior or harassment') does not name physical assault; with no assault leaf, SE-CONDUCT vs SE-OTHER is unclear for violence.

evidence.quote: the woman began hitting and scratching the driver's arm once again
Inappropriate behavior or harassment
The claimant says the driver's route

reason: Assault language triggers CLS-01 and SE-CONDUCT is the closest leaf. I drop my FC-ROUTE secondary because the claimant is the driver and FC-ROUTE requires that the claimant says the route made the trip longer.

evidence.quote: did not even pick him up from his location but he was charged for the trip nevertheless
The rider was charged a fare although the trip was completed without the rider onboard.

reason: Being charged for a trip without pickup is exactly FC-NOPICKUP; the driver's app excuse is context, not a separate claim.

evidence.quote: the ride and charge me
You didn't reply nor pick me up
The rider was charged a fare although the trip was completed without the rider onboard.

reason: The ride was marked complete and charged without pickup, so FC-NOPICKUP; a charge exists, so CW-DRIVERNOSHOW is excluded. Leaving the unreachable support line as context instead of my EX-OTHER secondary is acceptable.

evidence.quote: it was marked as completed, even though she was nowhere near my location.
in 54 seconds traveling 16 km
The rider was charged a fare although the trip was completed without the rider onboard.

reason: A 54-second, 16 km 'completed' trip charged to the card without pickup is FC-NOPICKUP. Support non-response as context rather than my EX-OTHER secondary is acceptable.

definition_issue: No FC leaf for a booked/upfront fare that differs from the fare the driver shows or charges; only the FC-OTHER catch-all takes it.

evidence.quote: his app indicated SGD14.10 (RM42) when he booked the ride
his screen showed the rate as SGD21.10 (RM64)
Other fare or charge issue

reason: The contested matter is a S$14.10 booked fare vs S$21.10 on the driver's screen, and no specific FC leaf (surge, toll, destination, payment) covers it. FC-OTHER is the correct catch-all, but the case needs a fare-mismatch type and lands in BACKLOG with no decision path.

definition_issue: No SE leaf for kidnapping/abduction or a route the rider perceives as unsafe, and 'kidnapping' is absent from CLS-01's word list.

evidence.quote: accused the former of kidnapping her on their trip from Bishan to the city
Other safety concern
safety language (assault, harassment, threats, unsafe driving, accident, injury, intoxication)

reason: A kidnapping allegation is a safety case with no specific SE leaf, so only the SE-OTHER catch-all fits. Every SE leaf is triaged to a human, so the gap does not change handling.

evidence.quote: the passenger replied that he would pay the S$18 fare via PayNow
the payment had not been made at all
unpaid fare or cash collection issues

reason: The driver claims an unpaid S$18 fare after a false PayNow payment, which is FC-PAYMENT (unpaid fare).

definition_issue: Whether CLS-02's 'safety claim (CLS-01)' covers SE leaves raised without CLS-01 words decides between SE-TERMINATED and the S$30 charge claim as primary; the off-app S$30 demand has no specific FC leaf (see C07).

evidence.quote: he cancelled the trip or finished something on the app, and he didn't bring us to Bedok
Ride terminated after the trip started
A safety claim (CLS-01) is always the primary claim

reason: The driver ended the trip midway and left the riders short of Bedok, which is SE-TERMINATED and, as an SE claim, primary. The S$30 demand as FC-PAYMENT is a defensible secondary (my FC-OTHER equally so).

definition_issue: FC-SURCHARGE's examples are official fees (Sentosa, Jurong Island, bulky item, wheelchair, child seat); a driver-invented 'VIP' charge fits only on the word 'surcharge', overlapping FC-OTHER.

evidence.quote: he had added a S$5 charge for 'VIP treatment'
the surcharge was never discussed or agreed upon
The claimant contests a surcharge or entry fee

reason: The rider contests a S$5 add-on the driver imposed, and the definition's core is 'contests a surcharge', so FC-SURCHARGE fits. FC-OTHER is the alternative; both are BACKLOG, so the choice is outcome-neutral.

evidence.quote: submitted a claim for the maximum S$120 reimbursement under Grab's cleaning fee policy
The driver claims a cleaning fee for a mess caused by the rider

reason: The driver claims a cleaning fee for rider vomit, rejected over the receipt, which is DM-CLEANING. CW-OTHER for the lost cancellation rate and streak incentives is a reasonable catch-all secondary.
